items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: We were in Chicago with the Bob Crosby band and the drummer was Ray Bauduc.

ctx.x: Well I’ve been doing it, let’s see 1939 is when it first happened. I got bitten by this big noise thing in 1939 it was actually. We were in Chicago with the Bob Crosby band and the drummer was Ray Bauduc. And he’s from New Orleans and a very colorful drummer.

He was the whole show and you’d go hear the show and you’d remember him because the way he played the drums, he was an act in himself. Wonderful. He could dance. But we were doing a number for the kids from Winnetka. There were a lot of kids from, it was a suburb of Chicago. The kids were in there to hear the band on a Sunday afternoon and we had a radio broadcast coming up as I remember it was at 5:00. And we used to put on a show for the kids with the small band, come down off the stand and had trumpet,…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: Haggard and I got together and I patterned it because I thought that those those those three tunes gave me enough positions or whatever you want to call it music

ctx.x: You're talking about how you patented on those three tunes.

Yeah, well, yeah, I was, I was, I used these three tunes, High Society and Panama and then Fidgety Feet. That was the three tunes that we got together, Haggard and I got together and I patterned it because I thought that those those those three tunes gave me enough positions or whatever you want to call it music that would represent a good good jazz band in New Orleans and then a good parade band see. items.q: when we got together with Haggard and wrote the thing out

ctx.x: Tied to that rig. And half of it was stretched to one side of the street, the other one to the other side of the street. Now, they got two guys to handle those ropes, see? One and one on each side. Mm-hmm. Now, they're strutting along, and this, this is leading the parade. And the band's come marching, and they're strutting along. Mm-hmm. And these two guys, they weren't worried about looking at the other guy on the other side. And they weren't, we're, we're looking at, at, at the, at the bull itself. But they…
I hear, I hear brass bands played in parades and everything.
